metadata.title: These signs suggest investors should give the software sector a second chance - MarketWatch

content.text:
Market Extra
These signs suggest investors should give the software sector a second chance
Software stocks and loans have started to find their footing in July, suggesting it may be time for investors to forgive and forget
Investors may have good reason to avoid the software sector — but some signs suggest the worst has passed, and that it may be time to start showing the group some love.
Software exposure had been the thing for investors to avoid after a treacherous start to the year. The roughly $2 trillion private-credit market has been awash in redemption requests, especially in funds with heavy industry exposure. Leveraged loans, which had helped finance the software boom into late 2025, have tumbled in price. And the iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF IGV had dropped nearly 40% from its record high in September through its April lows.
